C4-RESTORE(1)

NAME
    c4 restore - make a directory match a description, undo-safely

SYNOPSIS
    c4 restore <target> <dir>            (dry run: print the plan)
    c4 restore --force <target> <dir>    (snapshot dir, then apply)

    target:  a C4 ID resolved from the store (a snapshot ID, a content
             ID, or any stored listing ID, including a subdirectory's),
             a c4m file path (patch chains are resolved), or - (stdin).
             A directory is never a target.
    dir:     the directory to reconcile; created if absent.

DESCRIPTION
    Reconciles <dir> to match <target>: entries are created, moved,
    updated, and removed as needed. A snapshot-ID target restores
    recorded modes and times as well as content; a content-ID target
    restores byte-exact content with platform-default metadata. Content
    is pulled by ID from the store and from bytes already present in
    <dir> (moves are detected).

    Without --force, nothing is written. stdout is the plan in c4m
    patch format: the C4 ID of <dir>'s current state, the entries that
    differ, and the target's ID. The two boundary IDs always appear;
    when <dir> already matches, they are equal and no entries appear.

    With --force:
      1. Every ID the target names must be resolvable; otherwise the
         missing IDs are listed on stderr and restore exits 1 without
         touching <dir>.
      2. If <dir> contains anything a snapshot cannot fully record
         (unreadable files, sockets, fifos, devices), restore refuses,
         lists the offenders on stderr, and exits 1 without touching
         <dir>.
      3. <dir>'s current state is snapshotted into the store — content,
         listings, and journal entry, durable — and that pre-image
         snapshot ID is printed as stdout line 1, always before the
         first modification.
      4. <dir> is reconciled, then verified: the resulting tree must
         reproduce the target's ID by recomputation at the target's
         level of detail. Only then is the target ID printed as line 2.

UNDO
    Line 1 reverses the operation:
        c4 restore --force <line-1> <dir>
    restores <dir> byte-exact, including recorded modes and times. The
    undo prints its own line 1, so it is itself undoable. Every
    pre-image is listed in the store journal (`c4 log`), so a lost
    terminal does not lose the undo handle.

OUTPUT
    Dry run: the plan (c4m patch format) on stdout.
    --force: exactly two lines on stdout —
      line 1: pre-image snapshot ID of <dir> as it was
      line 2: the target's ID, verified from the resulting tree
    If <dir> already matches the target exactly, both lines are the
    same ID. If <dir> was absent or empty, line 1 is the empty
    description
    c459dsjfscH38cYeXXYogktxf4Cd9ibshE3BHUo6a58hBXmRQdZrAkZzsWcbWtDg5oQstpDuni4Hirj75GEmTc1sFT
    Restoring that ID empties the directory. Counts, warnings, and the
    undo command go to stderr.

DURABILITY
    Line 1 prints only after the pre-image is on stable media and
    always before the first modification. Line 2 prints only after the
    restored tree is verified and synced. If power fails between the
    lines, <dir> holds a mix of old and new whole files (no torn
    files); both end states are safe in the store — re-run the same
    command to finish, or restore line 1 to go back.

NOTES
    A description records names, sizes, modes, mtimes, symlink targets,
    hard links, sequences, and content IDs. It does not record
    ownership, extended attributes, ACLs, or special files; restore
    neither preserves nor restores those. Target entries with null IDs
    cannot be materialized: the rest is restored, the omissions are
    listed on stderr, and restore exits 2. restore never deletes <dir>
    itself: undoing a restore into a previously absent directory leaves
    an empty directory. Concurrent restores of the same directory are
    not coordinated: the store stays safe; the tree's final state is
    undefined.

EXIT STATUS
    0 plan emitted, or reconciled and verified
    1 refused: missing content, uncapturable entries, or unresolvable
      target — nothing modified
    2 reconciled with omissions (listed on stderr)

EXAMPLES

C4-CAT(1)

NAME
    c4 cat - retrieve store objects by ID; display c4m files

SYNOPSIS
    c4 cat [-e] [-r] <c4id | file.c4m>

DESCRIPTION
    With a C4 ID, fetches the object from the store and writes it to
    stdout. Every read is verified: the bytes must hash to the
    requested ID, or cat writes nothing and exits 1. A file ID yields
    the file's bytes. A listing ID (snapshot or content) yields the
    one-level child listing; with -r, directory entries are followed by
    their own listings, indented two spaces per level, fetched from the
    store. A c4m file path displays the file; patch chains display
    resolved (use c4 log for history).

FLAGS
    -e, --ergonomic   Column-aligned c4m output
    -r, --recursive   Expand directory entries through the store

EXAMPLES
    c4 cat c461iQnu...igYz                 # one-level listing
    c4 cat -r c461iQnu...igYz              # whole tree, from the store
    c4 cat -r c461iQnu...igYz | c4 paths   # all paths
    c4 cat -r c461iQnu...igYz | grep ' report.pdf '   # find a file's ID
    c4 cat c45PDQdg...UNN > hello.txt      # extract one file
    c4 cat -r ID | c4 id -q -              # recompute: verifies ID

C4-PATCH(1) / C4-DIFF(1)

SYNOPSIS
    c4 patch [-n N] [-e] <chain.c4m> [<dest.c4m>]
    c4 patch [-n N] [-e] <file.c4m>...
    c4 diff [-e] <old> <new>

DESCRIPTION
    patch resolves patch chains: c4m text in, resolved c4m text out
    (stdout, or <dest.c4m>). patch reads and writes c4m text only; a
    directory argument exits 1 with:
        patch composes descriptions; to change a directory:
        c4 restore <target> <dir>
    -n N resolves to section N (1-based; 0 = final state).

    diff compares two states and emits a patch on stdout. Either side
    may be a directory, a c4m file, or a stored description ID.
    Directories are scanned at content level, or at the other side's
    level of detail when that side is a description.

C4-LOG(1)

NAME
    c4 log - list a patch chain's sections; default: the store journal

SYNOPSIS
    c4 log [<chain.c4m>...]

DESCRIPTION
    Lists one line per section: index, entry fields, section ID. With
    no arguments, reads the store journal <store>/log.c4m, in which the
    store records every ingest: snapshots from `c4 id -s`, stdin blobs
    from `| c4 -s`, and every pre-image taken by `c4 restore --force`.
    Each journal section is one entry:

        - <time> <listing-size> <name>.c4m <- <host:abs-path> <snapshot-id>

    followed by the chain boundary line. The journal is ordinary c4m
    text: any text tool can read it, and nothing in it is ever
    overwritten — history only. Appends are serialized with a lock; an
    interrupted append leaves an incomplete final line, which readers
    report on stderr and the next append repairs.

EXAMPLES
    c4 log                            # every snapshot this store holds
    c4 log /backup/store/log.c4m      # another store's journal

C4-GC(1)

NAME
    c4 gc - collect store objects unreachable from the roots

SYNOPSIS
    c4 gc [--force] [-v] [<roots.c4m>...]

DESCRIPTION
    Mark-and-sweep. Dry run unless --force. The roots are every ID
    recorded in any section of the store journal — full history, their
    listings at both levels of detail, and everything those name — plus
    any c4m files given as arguments. Arguments add roots; they never
    replace the journal roots, so nothing journaled is ever collected.
    To let old snapshots go, first truncate the journal explicitly:
        c4 split <store>/log.c4m <N> archive.c4m keep.c4m
    install keep.c4m as the journal (with snapshot activity stopped),
    then run c4 gc --force.

FLAGS
    --force     Delete unreferenced objects (default: report only)
    -v          List each unreferenced object

ledger.item: Two user-visible identity concepts: content ID and snapshot ID, one sentence each
ledger.reason: Unanimous across candidates and the provable minimum: T3 needs machine-independent sameness, T1/T2 need exact-record fidelity; no single ID answers both.

ledger.item: Content-form (stat-free) directory identity as the default for c4 id (-m c default)
ledger.reason: Fixes the standing determinism violation (same bytes, two machines, two IDs) and is the only way T3 is answerable by string equality; uses frozen nulls, zero grammar change; observation stays one flag away (-m f).

ledger.item: Stat-bearing directory ID retained as any default identity
ledger.reason: Violates principle 10 (IDs reproduce across machines/umasks/clocks) and answers no question content ID + snapshot ID don't answer better; drift detection is diff's job.

ledger.item: Snapshot ID = ID of the full-observation root listing (flatten rule: description's canonical-text ID == root directory ID at the same knowledge level)
ledger.reason: A's found unification, verified against shipped WriteCanonical; makes self-ID, pipe law, and round-trip verification one rule and one object kind.

ledger.item: Separate whole-text description blob as the snapshot object (B/C mechanism)
ledger.reason: Mints a second object kind, invites the key-collision B itself documented, and loses per-directory Merkle dedup of descriptions; the flatten unification makes it unnecessary.

ledger.item: Snapshot ingestion stores BOTH listing graphs (full-form and content-form) per directory
ledger.reason: Makes cat/restore resolve either ID with no index or projection machinery; listing objects are tiny; closes the content-ID-resolution gap prosecutors found in A.

ledger.item: Full-form listings carry child full-listing IDs; content-form carry child content IDs (line-local verification both graphs)
ledger.reason: Every ID in any listing is the hash of the exact text it names; dissolves the 'invisible null-form transform' count against C.

ledger.item: Directory size field = total bytes of contained files, both forms
ledger.reason: st_size for directories is filesystem-dependent and would re-taint the content ID; sum is deterministic and informative (C advocate's fix).

ledger.item: Description-input dispatch pinned: .c4m argument and id's '-' parse as descriptions; unparseable .c4m errors; all other files are bytes; bare c4 stdin is raw bytes
ledger.reason: Kills content-sniffing (looksLikeC4m) nondeterminism convicted in A count 1; dispatch is a pure function of the argument name.

ledger.item: Files inside scanned trees are ALWAYS bytes — never parsed, canonicalized, or re-ID'd
ledger.reason: The shipped scan-time canonicalization (id.go:250-268) silently corrupts trees containing c4m-shaped files and falsifies T1 byte-exactness; hard-pinned on the surface.

ledger.item: id computes descriptions at their own knowledge level; -m projects downward only
ledger.reason: Restores snapshot-ID recomputability from a file in hand (B blocking count 2) while preserving the pipe law and the cat -r round-trip verify (both hit the same rule via the flatten identity).

ledger.item: Patch chains resolve to final state before identification/display; -n reaches earlier states
ledger.reason: Pins the previously undefined chain-identity case deterministically using an existing flag.

ledger.item: -q requires an ID-bearing mode (c or f); errors under -m s/m
ledger.reason: An ID printed from bytes never hashed would be assertion, not verification (C prosecutor count 10).

ledger.item: id -s prints the snapshot ID alone on stdout; narration on stderr
ledger.reason: The ID is the machine datum and stdout is data (B's stderr-only 'recorded:' channel convicted under principle 9); the description text is exactly the losable artifact of complaint 1 and lives in the store instead.

ledger.item: id -s conflicts with -m (always full detail; content projection stored alongside)
ledger.reason: One canonical -s behavior; A's 'id -s -m c' variant subsumed since the content graph is always stored and the content ID always derivable.

ledger.item: Bare 'c4 <path>' is read-only (alias for id); nothing stores without -s; stdin auto-store removed; -x deleted
ledger.reason: REJECTED: bare-invocation auto-ingest. A cold user asking 'what is this?' must not silently write gigabytes (A prosecutor count 6); uniform rule 'writes require -s or restore --force' replaces the -x escape flag. Breaking pre-freeze change, deliberate.

ledger.item: Store journal <store>/log.c4m exists: ordinary c4m patch chain, one section per -s ingest (snapshots, stdin blobs, and every restore pre-image, including empty pre-images)
ledger.reason: A's no-log design was convicted (undo handle only on ephemeral stdout; store cannot name its own roots); logging every -s closes B's lone-file-unrooted gc deletion; 'logged iff stored-at-your-request iff gc-protected' is one teachable sentence.

ledger.item: Journal read as history only via 'c4 log' (no-arg default); catalog resolution as the undo flow
ledger.reason: REJECTED: catalog semantics. Basename-keyed current-state resolution hands the user the WRONG pre-image on name collision (B blocking 3 / C blocking 1) — the safety feature becomes the destroyer; history listing evicts nothing and log is the verb named for it.

ledger.item: Bare 'c4 patch' as the catalog/recovery entry point
ledger.reason: Undiscoverable and mis-signaled: cold users will not run an apparently mutating verb with no arguments to read state (B prosecutor count 12).

ledger.item: Journal torn-tail handling: writers repair under advisory lock before appending; readers warn on stderr (uniform c4m trailing-garbage behavior)
ledger.reason: Keeps the at-rest file valid c4m with zero grammar change; avoids B's location-specific silent-drop parse dialect (identical bytes must parse identically everywhere).

ledger.item: Journal appends serialized by advisory lock; store puts concurrent-safe by construction (temp+fsync+rename, put-by-ID)
ledger.reason: Pins the concurrency semantics C left unspecified at the exact file the durability contract rests on.

ledger.item: Durability protocol: temp+fsync(2)+rename per object; barrier; journal append+fsync; barrier; then print. Printed => durable; unprinted => nothing claimed, tree untouched, store consistent, rerun idempotent
ledger.reason: Convergent across candidates and grounded in measured physics (~2.5s + ~11ms for 20k files); per-file fsync is what keeps dedup's presence-implies-integrity valid after a crash.

ledger.item: Per-file F_FULLFSYNC durability
ledger.reason: Measured ~6.4ms/file (~3 minutes per 20k files) and buys nothing over the claim-point barrier; a promise nobody can act on.

ledger.item: Durability contract worded platform-neutrally; APFS/M-series numbers cited as measurements
ledger.reason: B prosecutor count 9: F_FULLFSYNC-specific semantics must not be the contract; Linux implementation supplies the equivalent barrier (fsync of files and containing directories).

ledger.item: Restored trees get the strong promise: per-file fsync+rename, verify by recomputation at the target's knowledge level, barrier, then line 2 prints
ledger.reason: C's 'no tree durability promise' rejected as under-promising when the strong claim costs ~126us/file; A's verify-then-print adopted; between-lines state pinned as mix of whole files with both endpoints durable.

ledger.item: --no-fsync flag (anywhere)
ledger.reason: Safe was made fast (~126us/file), so the mode would only multiply crash states; 'fast by flag' is satisfied by the defaults.

ledger.item: restore is the ONLY tree-writing verb; patch returns to pure text algebra and errors on directories with a teaching message
ledger.reason: One implementation per idea; deletes the accident grammar of complaint 2 rather than surviving it; B's 8-way patch dispatch and 'patch <dir>' second spelling of id -s convicted under principles 1 and 12.

ledger.item: restore is dry-run by default; --force applies (the single new flag)
ledger.reason: Principle 8's literal text ('dry-run defaults'), the shipped gc --force precedent, and the founding wrong-usage user all favor plan-first; A's zero-flag always-apply rejected because its invertibility claim has holes (incomplete pre-images) and it breaks suite consistency.

ledger.item: Dry-run plan output: boundary IDs always present, equal with no entries when already matching
ledger.reason: Fixes C's self-contradiction between 'empty output means matching' and the stated plan format; scripts get one parseable contract, and the plan's first line is exactly what --force will print.

ledger.item: --force stdout = two lines: pre-image snapshot ID (durable, before first mutation) then verified target ID
ledger.reason: Merges A's two-line undo/redo contract into C's gating; 'backups durable before destruction begins' is the meaning of line 1, not a flag.

ledger.item: No opt-out of the pre-image; --no-store broadened to skip it
ledger.reason: REJECTED: --no-store broadening. Inheriting destructiveness into a benign shipped flag is the opposite of long-form-explicit (B prosecutor count 5); the case where the pre-image is expensive is the case it exists for; rm -rf remains the honest capture-free spelling.

ledger.item: --force refuses (exit 1, offenders listed, nothing touched) when <dir> contains entries a snapshot cannot fully capture (unreadable files, sockets/fifos/devices)
ledger.reason: Resolves A blocking count 2: destruction demands complete capture; description alone stays partial-friendly (id warns, records nulls, exits 2), so principle 11 is honored where reading is concerned and principle 8 where destroying is.

ledger.item: Fidelity boundary stated on the surface: records names/sizes/modes/mtimes/symlinks/hardlinks/sequences/content; NOT ownership/xattrs/ACLs/special files
ledger.reason: C prosecutor count 2: 'byte-exact including recorded metadata' must not overpromise; whatever c4m cannot describe, c4 promises nowhere; sidecar can extend later.

ledger.item: gc default roots = every ID in ANY journal section (full history, both graphs, closures); explicit c4m args ADD roots, never replace; forgetting = explicit journal truncation via split, then gc --force
ledger.reason: Closes A's gc-collects-undo-history contradiction and decides C's history-vs-current root ambiguity in favor of history; retention stays an explicit composition, never a policy.

ledger.item: restore targets are descriptions only (ID, .c4m, or -); directory targets; dir-to-dir mirroring = restore --force $(c4 id -s A) B with the missing-content trap named in the man page
ledger.reason: Direction confusion ('which side wins') becomes unconstructible; the -s requirement and its reason (content must be in the store) are stated where a cold user will hit them.

ledger.item: --source flag on restore (content from arbitrary directories, store-bypass mirroring)
ledger.reason: No success task needs it; store-mediated transfer is the architecture and same-volume clonefile ingest is ~free (0.26s/14k measured); preserves one flag of budget headroom. Revisit only with measured pain (C prosecutor count 3 acknowledged, deferred with reason).

ledger.item: Empty description constant as pre-image of absent/empty dirs; undo of restore-into-absent-dir leaves an empty directory (restore never deletes <dir> itself); no-op forced restore prints the same ID twice
ledger.reason: One always-resolvable fixed point replaces three special cases; the one-inode boundary is stated honestly instead of overclaimed (A prosecutor count 9).

ledger.item: Concurrent restores of one directory: uncoordinated, stated on the surface (store safe, tree outcome undefined)
ledger.reason: Prosecutors flagged the silence; one honest sentence beats an unstated assumption for first-class agent users.

ledger.item: Journal entry format: '- <UTC time> <listing size> <name>.c4m <- <host:abs-path> <snapshot ID>' + chain boundary per section
ledger.reason: C's provenance flow link (frozen grammar) makes entries self-explanatory and disambiguates same-basename trees by origin path; collisions are harmless under history-only semantics.

ledger.item: Legacy stat-bearing listings/IDs: remain valid full-form listing objects that verify as the hash of their own text; content IDs re-derived by c4 id -q; no permanent dual-rule verifier
ledger.reason: Under the merged model legacy IDs ARE full-form IDs, so nothing dangles; migration is one recompute, and mixed-fleet T3 is governed by the coordinated suite release (design-doc note, not user surface).

ledger.item: Multi-store config: first store is the write store and holds the journal
ledger.reason: Pins C's 'store line(s) plural' ambiguity in one sentence.

ledger.item: id/id -s exit 2 on partial scans (unreadable entries recorded with null IDs, listed on stderr); restore exits 2 when target null-ID entries were skipped
ledger.reason: Partial knowledge stays a valid, LOUD state: degraded output plus a distinct exit code, so T1-affecting gaps are never silent.

ledger.item: Journal semantics for non-local (s3/remote) stores
ledger.reason: Networking/daemon is a declared non-goal; this surface claims local stores only. Non-blocking.

ledger.item: Retention recipe concurrency (stop writers during split; gc holds the append lock while rooting)
ledger.reason: GC policy is a declared non-goal; the root rule shipped here is safe-by-default and the surgery recipe is explicitly manual. Non-blocking implementation note.

ledger.item: Exact c4 log column layout and narration wording
ledger.reason: Cosmetic; may be adjusted after blind-sim feedback without semantic change. Non-blocking.

# c4 snapshot–store–restore — Draft v2 (round-1 fold)

## Round-1 fold summary

Four blind personas (cold developer, 15-year git user, autonomous agent, skeptical HN skimmer) ran the five success tasks cold: **20/20 succeeded**. Zero round-1 prosecutor blocking counts remain unresolved. Nine distinct novel friction events surfaced; every one is folded below or accepted into the ledger. Two are design changes; the rest are exactness fixes:

1. **ID/path store addressing** (design change; friction: "no find-by-path primitive; grep-and-hope lookup"). Store-reading verbs accept `<ID>/relative/path`, descending stored listings by exact entry name, one hash-verified level at a time. Zero new flags, zero new verbs — thin sugar over the documented listing walk.
2. **Journal-line durability equivalence + pinned repair** (design change; friction: "'trust me, it self-heals' with zero specifics"). A complete journal line found after a crash names a fully durable snapshot, because everything it references was barriered before the line was appended; a torn tail is the residue of an ingest that never claimed success; repair = truncate the trailing partial section under the append lock. Worst case stated.
3. Exactness fixes: `id -s` side effects enumerated (store only, nothing else, ever); `-q` framed as output form, never identity selection; restore verification defined per knowledge level and "platform-default metadata" defined; the timing model reconciled against its own transcript (durability overhead vs hash-bound total); the SHA-512 axiom stated once; progress narration on stderr; "the journal is the reflog" stated where a git user looks for refs.

## Verdict shape

Two properties carry the design, the first now readable from both sides:

1. **The print barrier.** A snapshot ID reaches stdout only after everything ingest stored — file bytes, listings, and the journal entry — is on stable media. Printed means durable; unprinted means nothing was claimed: the source tree was never written to, the store's prior contents are intact, and rerun is idempotent (dedup skips existing objects). New in v2: the claim is verifiable from the store side too — **any complete journal line found after a crash names a fully durable snapshot** (its objects were barriered before the append began); a torn tail can only belong to an ingest that never printed.
2. **The journal.** The store names its own roots. Every `-s` ingest (snapshots, stdin blobs, every `restore --force` pre-image, including empty ones) appends one section to `<store>/log.c4m`, an ordinary c4m patch chain. `c4 log` with no arguments lists it. This rescues the complaint-#2 user whose scrollback is gone and closes complaint #1's deepest form ("the ID itself is also losable"). There is deliberately **no ref namespace**: handles are IDs; the journal is the reflog.

## 1. Identity — one mechanism, two named knowledge levels

There is exactly one naming rule (frozen): the C4 ID of canonical bytes; for a directory, the bytes are the one-level canonical listing of its direct children. The design pins which observation fields populate the listing — a semantics choice the frozen grammar's first-class nulls already permit — and names the two levels users need:

- **content ID** — listing with mode and timestamp null; names, sizes, symlink targets, and child *content* IDs real. Equal iff contents are byte-identical, on any machine, clock, or umask. **The default level for `c4 id`.** Answers T3 by string equality.
- **snapshot ID** — listing with everything observed; directory entries carry child *full-listing* IDs, so every ID in a full listing is line-locally recomputable from the object it names. Printed by `c4 id -s`; the recovery handle.

Directory size field = total bytes of contained files in both forms (deterministic; never st_size). A single file's snapshot ID and content ID coincide (its bytes). Flatten rule: a description's own canonical-text ID equals its root ID at its own knowledge level — so the pipe law (`c4 id DIR | c4 id -q -` prints DIR's content ID) and snapshot-ID recomputability (`c4 id -q saved.c4m`; `c4 cat -r SNAP | c4 id -q -`) are the *same* rule.

v2 pins from sim friction:

- **`-q` is output form, never identity selection.** What is identified is chosen by `-m` (default: content). `c4 id -q dir` is machine-independent because content is the default level, not because of `-q`; `-q` only suppresses the c4m text in favor of the bare ID. Stated in help and man page — kills the git-user inversion ("I must opt into the stable hash via a flag").
- **The hash axiom, stated once.** ID equality is SHA-512 equality: distinct byte streams share an ID only by a SHA-512 collision — the axiom every content-addressed claim in c4 rests on, stated once rather than hedged per line. Reads never extend that trust: every object fetched from the store is rehashed against the requested ID. (Ledger-accepted tradeoff.)

Dispatch pinned, no sniffing (unchanged from v1): a top-level argument ending in `.c4m`, and `-` on `id`, parse as descriptions (unparseable `.c4m` = error, never silently hashed); every other file argument is bytes; **files inside a scanned tree are always bytes** — never parsed, canonicalized, or re-ID'd. Bare `c4` with piped stdin identifies raw bytes. Patch chains resolve to their final state before identification (`patch -n` reaches earlier states).

## 2. Self-description — the store alone recovers everything, and is addressable

`c4 id -s DIR` is a total ingest: file bytes; per-directory full-form listings (the snapshot graph, root included); per-directory content-form listings (so content IDs also resolve via `cat`/`restore`); one journal section. Listings are tiny text objects; both graphs dedup across snapshots (unchanged subtrees reuse objects — O(changes) history with no history feature). There is no separate description blob (rejected in v1: second object kind, key-collision hazard; under the flatten unification the description *is* the root listing). Ingesting a description (`c4 id -s x.c4m`, `c4 patch chain | c4 id -s -`) stores its listings; referenced content is not thereby stored — partial knowledge is first-class, and `restore` pre-flights the closure.

v2 pins from sim friction:

- **Side effects enumerated.** `id -s` writes only inside the store directory: content objects, listing objects, one journal section. It creates no files anywhere else — no `.c4m` file, nothing in the scanned tree, nothing in the working directory, ever. stdout is the ID; stderr is narration. (Two personas' worst confusion was doubt about exactly this; one sentence on the surface ends it.)
- **ID/path addressing.** Anywhere a store-resolved ID is accepted (`cat`, `restore` targets, `diff` sides), the ID may be followed by a slash-separated relative path: `c4 cat SNAP/src/parser.go`. Each component descends one level by exact entry-name match in the stored listing; every fetched object is verified by rehash; the final component may name a file (bytes) or a directory (its listing). Works at either knowledge level. This is sugar over the documented walk (cat the listing → read the entry's ID → cat that ID) and replaces the fragile `cat -r | grep ' name '` idiom as the documented lookup (the raw composition remains valid). Unknown component ⇒ exit 1, missing name on stderr. Not a third identity concept: it is an addressing form that resolves to an entry's existing ID. Edge semantics (symlink components, trailing slash, `.c4m`-file targets) are round-2 items.
- **Progress narration.** stderr carries progress: a live file/byte count on a terminal, a single summary line otherwise. stdout stays byte-pure (the ID and nothing else).

Journal semantics: **history only** (catalog resolution stays rejected — basename collisions handed users the wrong pre-image). Entry format unchanged: `- <UTC time> <listing size> <name>.c4m <- <host:abs-path> <snapshot ID>` plus the chain boundary. Discovery is `c4 log` (no-arg default), which lists every section, evicting nothing.

## 3. Durability — printed means durable; journaled means durable; measured, not aspirational

Protocol (unchanged): objects land temp-file + fsync(2) + atomic rename (~126 µs/file; presence under a final name implies integrity, keeping dedup's Has() valid after a crash); one device flush barrier; journal append + fsync; second barrier; then the ID prints and exit 0. Per-file F_FULLFSYNC stays rejected (measured ~6.4 ms/file, ~3 min per 20k files, buys nothing over the claim-point barrier). `--no-fsync` stays deleted everywhere.

v2 pins from sim friction:

- **Arithmetic reconciled on the surface.** "Overhead" is durability overhead *beyond reading and hashing the data, which dominate*: ~130 µs/file plus two ~5 ms barriers. The transcript's run reconciles explicitly: 20,312 files / 4.8 GB ⇒ ~3.5 s to read and hash + ~2.6 s durability overhead ≈ 6.1 s total. One model, one transcript, consistent — the HN sim's "numbers contradict by 2×" dissolves because the man page now states what the constant excludes and shows the sum.
- **Constants are measurements, the contract is ordering.** Figures are from one machine (Apple-silicon APFS SSD); other filesystems change the constants, never the ordering contract: synced before renamed; barriered before journaled; journaled before printed. Linux supplies the equivalent (fsync of files and containing directories plus a device flush).
- **Journal-line equivalence.** If power fails between the journal barrier and the print, whatever `c4 log` shows after reboot is real: a complete journal line names a fully durable snapshot, verifiable in one pipe (`c4 cat -r ID | c4 id -q -`); the command merely never claimed it.
- **Torn-tail repair pinned.** Writers hold the advisory lock and truncate any trailing partial section before appending; readers parse complete sections and warn once on stderr about a tail. Worst case: if no append ever follows, the tail persists harmlessly and every complete section stays readable — a torn tail can only be the residue of an ingest that never printed, so nothing claimed is ever lost. Objects staged by an unclaimed ingest are unrooted: `gc` dry-run lists them; rerunning the ingest claims them.

Materialization keeps the strong promise: restored files are written temp+fsync+rename; the target ID prints only after the tree is verified by recomputation at the target's knowledge level and one barrier completes. Between restore's two output lines, the tree may hold a mix of old and new whole files — both endpoints are already durable in the store; re-run to finish or restore line 1 to go back.

## 4. Destructive reconcile — one tree-writer, plan by default, pre-image before destruction

`c4 restore <target> <dir>` is the only verb that writes working trees. `patch` is pure text algebra and errors on directory arguments with a message that teaches `restore`. Unchanged from v1: dry-run default with pinned plan output (boundary IDs always present; equal, with no entries, when already matching); `--force` = pre-flight the closure (missing content ⇒ stderr list, exit 1, touch nothing) → full-fidelity pre-image through the total-ingest protocol, durable and journaled **before the first destructive operation**, printed as stdout line 1 → reconcile → verify → target ID as line 2; completeness gate (refuse, listing offenders, when `<dir>` holds entries the pre-image cannot fully capture); no pre-image opt-out (`rm -rf` remains the honest capture-free spelling); fidelity boundary stated on the surface (records names/sizes/modes/mtimes/symlinks/hardlinks/sequences/content IDs — not ownership/xattrs/ACLs/special files); empty-description constant as pre-image of absent/empty dirs (restore never deletes `<dir>` itself); targets are descriptions only (ID — now optionally ID/path — `.c4m`, or `-`); mirroring = `restore --force $(c4 id -s A) B` with the missing-content trap named; `--source` stays rejected (one flag of headroom deliberately preserved); concurrent restores of one directory uncoordinated — store safe, tree outcome undefined (ledger-accepted tradeoff; re-flagged by a sim, stands).

v2 pins from sim friction:

- **Verification defined per knowledge level.** Snapshot-ID target: recorded modes and mtimes are applied explicitly (creation umask is irrelevant), then the full-form listing graph is recomputed from the resulting tree and must reproduce the snapshot ID. Content-ID target: the content-form graph is recomputed and must reproduce the content ID — names, sizes, symlink targets, and bytes are verified; modes and times are **platform-default metadata**, defined as whatever file creation under your umask and clock produced — not recorded by the target, not claimed, not verified. Line 2 prints only if recomputation reproduces the target ID exactly.
- **No ref namespace, said where git users look for it.** The undo handle is the pre-image ID itself: stdout line 1, echoed in the stderr undo hint as a complete command, and recorded permanently in the journal — `c4 log` is the reflog. Nothing to update, nothing to lose.

**GC coherence** (unchanged): default roots = every ID appearing in any journal section — full history, both listing graphs, and their closures; explicit c4m arguments add roots, never replace. Nothing journaled is ever collectable until the journal is explicitly truncated (`split`, then `gc --force`). v2 adds: unjournaled objects from an unclaimed ingest are unrooted by construction — the dry run names them. Retention policy remains a non-goal.

## Surface accounting (honest)

Within budget: **2 identity concepts** (content ID, snapshot ID); **1 new verb** (`restore`); **1 new flag** (`--force` on restore; 1 of 2 spent). Ledgered non-flag surface from v1: mode value `c` on existing `-m` (new default); `id -q`/`id -s` output redefinitions (breaking, pre-freeze, deliberate); bare `c4 <path>` read-only; stdin no longer auto-stores; one well-known file `<store>/log.c4m`; no-arg default on `log`. **New ledgered non-flag surface in v2:** ID/path addressing on store-resolved IDs (an addressing form, not an identity concept); stderr progress narration (non-contractual). Deletions unchanged: `id -x`; `patch -s/-r/-q/--dry-run/--source/--no-store/--no-fsync/-m` and all directory forms; `diff -r/-s/-q` — net flag count still falls by roughly nine. 0 grammar changes; 0 dependencies; stdout byte-pure everywhere.

## Migration notes (design-level, unchanged)

Legacy stat-bearing listings remain valid full-form listing objects that verify as the hash of their own text; nothing dangles. Content IDs re-derive in one command (`c4 id -q`). Mixed-version fleets answer T3 only when both ends run the suite that ships content-default IDs — governed by the coordinated suite release (RELEASE.md); this identity default is the launch gate.

## Task closure (v2)

- T1: `SNAP=$(c4 id -s proj/)` — writes nothing outside the store, so "files produced outside the store" is the empty set *by construction, now stated on the surface*; `rm -rf proj/`; a lost ID is re-supplied by `c4 log`; `c4 restore --force SNAP proj/` rebuilds byte-exact with metadata, verified before line 2 prints.
- T2: the accident's own stdout line 1 (or `c4 log`) names the victim's pre-image; one `restore --force` returns it byte-exact; the undo prints its own line 1, so it is itself undoable.
- T3: `c4 id -q dir` on each machine; string-equal iff byte-identical (content is the default level; `-q` merely quiets output).
- T4: ~6 s for 20k files / 4.8 GB (~3.5 s read+hash + ~2.6 s durability). Printed ⇒ snapshot, content, and journal entry survive power loss. Journal line present but unprinted ⇒ snapshot durable and discoverable via `c4 log`. Otherwise ⇒ nothing claimed, tree untouched, store consistent, rerun resumes.
- T5: `c4 cat SNAP` lists one level; `c4 cat SNAP/src/parser.go > parser.go` extracts by name (verified at every level); `cat -r | grep` remains the raw composition; `c4 cat -r SNAP | c4 id -q -` falsifies or confirms in one pipe.

## Open (for round 2)

1. ID/path edge semantics: a component that names a symlink or file mid-path; trailing-slash form; whether `.c4m`-file targets may take `/path`.
2. Journal entry naming for stdin blobs (`| c4 -s`): what fills the `<name>.c4m` and origin fields.
3. stderr progress line format and TTY detection heuristics (cosmetic; narration is non-contractual).
4. Exact `c4 log` column layout (cosmetic; survived sims unchanged).
5. Journal semantics for non-local (s3/remote) stores — networking is a non-goal; this surface claims local stores only.
6. Retention recipe concurrency (stop writers during `split`; gc holds the append lock while rooting) — implementation detail under a declared non-goal.
7. Fidelity sidecar for xattrs/ownership/ACLs — future external structure per the sidecar doctrine.

only after everything it stored is on stable media. The store records
every snapshot in its journal: run `c4 log` to list them.

Store: set C4_STORE=/path/to/store, or list stores in ~/.c4/config (the
first store is written to and holds the journal). Default: ~/.c4/store

C4-ID(1)

NAME
    c4 id - describe files and directories as c4m text; snapshot with -s

SYNOPSIS
    c4 id [-q] [-s] [-m s|c|m|f] [-e] [-S] [--exclude GLOB]...
          [--exclude-file FILE] [-c GUIDE] <path>...
    c4 id [-q] [-m MODE] -          (parse stdin as a c4m description)

DESCRIPTION
    Writes a plain-text c4m description of each path to stdout. Without
    -s, id reads only; nothing is written anywhere.

    With -s, id also stores a complete snapshot in the configured store:
    every file's bytes, every directory's one-level listing (root
    included, at both full and content detail), and one entry in the
    store journal. -s writes only inside the store directory: it creates
    no .c4m file, nothing in the scanned tree, nothing in your working
    directory. stdout is then a single line — the snapshot ID — printed
    only after everything stored is on stable media. Narration and
    progress go to stderr: a live file/byte count on a terminal, one
    summary line otherwise.

MODES (-m)
    s  structure   names only (no IDs)
    c  content     names, sizes, symlink targets, IDs computed from
                   bytes alone; mode and timestamp null (-). Default.
    m  metadata    modes, times, sizes, names (no IDs)
    f  full        everything observed
    -q requires a mode that records IDs (c or f). -s always records
    full detail and conflicts with -m.

IDENTITY
    A file's content ID is the ID of its bytes. A directory's ID is the
    ID of the one-level canonical listing of its direct children; with
    stat fields null this is its content ID (identical on every
    machine); with observed modes and times it is a snapshot ID. In a
    content-form listing, directory entries carry child content IDs; in
    a full-form listing, child full-listing IDs — every ID in a listing
    is the ID of the exact text of the object it names. A directory's
    size field is the total bytes of the files it contains. A single
    file's snapshot ID and content ID coincide: the ID of its bytes.
    ID equality is SHA-512 equality: distinct byte streams share an ID
    only by a SHA-512 collision, and every store read is rehashed
    against the requested ID rather than trusted.
    The ID of the empty description (and of zero bytes) is
    c459dsjfscH38cYeXXYogktxf4Cd9ibshE3BHUo6a58hBXmRQdZrAkZzsWcbWtDg5oQstpDuni4Hirj75GEmTc1sFT

DESCRIPTIONS AS INPUT
    An argument ending in .c4m, and `-`, are parsed as descriptions;
    a .c4m argument that does not parse is an error. All other file
    arguments are bytes. Files inside a scanned tree are always treated
    as bytes, whatever their name — never parsed or rewritten. A patch
    chain given to id resolves to its final state first (use
    `c4 patch -n N` for earlier states).

    For a description, id computes at the description's own level of
    detail, so its printed ID is the description's own canonical ID
    (for a full description, its snapshot ID). -m c projects a fuller
    description down to content form; fields cannot be added, only
    nulled. Ingesting a description with -s stores its listings; it
    does not store content the description refers to.

FLAGS
    -q, --quiet          Print only the C4 ID, one line per path.
                         -q changes output form, never identity: the
                         level identified is chosen by -m (default:
                         content). `c4 id -q dir` is machine-independent
                         because content is the default, not because
                         of -q.
    -s, --store          Snapshot into the store and print the snapshot
                         ID (implies -q)
    -m, --mode MODE      Scan detail: s, c, m, f (see MODES)
    -e, --ergonomic      Column-aligned output
    -S, --sequence       Detect and fold file sequences
    --exclude GLOB       Exclude pattern (repeatable)
    --exclude-file FILE  File of exclude patterns, one per line
    -c, --continue C4M   Use an existing c4m as a scan guide

DURABILITY
    If the snapshot ID printed, the snapshot — content, listings, and
    its journal entry — survives power loss, even one microsecond after
    printing. If it did not print, nothing was claimed: the scanned tree
    was never written to, the store's prior contents and journal are
    intact, and re-running the same command continues where it left off
    (objects already present are skipped). One in-between case exists:
    if power failed after the journal entry but before the print, the
    snapshot is complete and durable and `c4 log` lists it — whatever
    the journal shows after a crash is real.

    Objects are written to a temporary name, synced, and atomically
    renamed; a device flush barrier precedes the journal entry and a
    second precedes the printed ID. Durability overhead — beyond
    reading and hashing the data, which dominate — is roughly 130
    microseconds per file plus two ~5 ms barriers, measured on an
    Apple-silicon APFS SSD. Worked example: 20,312 files, 4.8 GB is
    about 3.5 s to read and hash plus about 2.6 s of durability
    overhead, roughly 6 s total. On other filesystems the constants
    differ; the ordering contract (synced before renamed, barriered
    before journaled, journaled before printed) does not.

PARTIAL SCANS
    An unreadable file is reported on stderr and recorded with a null
    ID; sockets, fifos, and devices are reported and omitted. The
    description (or snapshot) is still produced, and id exits 2.

FILES
    Store root: $C4_STORE, or the first store in ~/.c4/config, or
    ~/.c4/store. Journal: <store>/log.c4m — an ordinary c4m patch
    chain; one section per ingest. See c4-log(1).

EXIT STATUS
    0 success; 1 error; 2 partial scan (details on stderr)

EXAMPLES
    c4 id src/ > src.c4m            # describe (content form); no store
    c4 id -m f src/                 # full description with modes/times
    c4 id -q src/                   # content ID: same on every machine
    c4 id -s src/                   # snapshot; prints snapshot ID
    c4 id -q saved.c4m              # a saved description's own ID
    c4 id src/ | c4 id -q -         # pipe law: prints src's content ID
    c4 patch chain.c4m | c4 id -s - # store a resolved description

SEE ALSO
    c4 restore (materialize), c4 cat (read), c4 log (journal),
    c4 diff (compare), c4 gc (collect), c4 explain id

C4-RESTORE(1)

NAME
    c4 restore - make a directory match a description, undo-safely

SYNOPSIS
    c4 restore <target> <dir>            (dry run: print the plan)
    c4 restore --force <target> <dir>    (snapshot dir, then apply)

    target:  a C4 ID resolved from the store (a snapshot ID, a content
             ID, or any stored listing ID), optionally followed by
             /path to descend into it by entry name (e.g. SNAP/src); a
             c4m file path (patch chains are resolved); or - (stdin).
             A directory is never a target.
    dir:     the directory to reconcile; created if absent.

DESCRIPTION
    Reconciles <dir> to match <target>: entries are created, moved,
    updated, and removed as needed. A snapshot-ID target restores
    recorded modes and times as well as content; a content-ID target
    restores byte-exact content with platform-default metadata (see
    VERIFICATION). Content is pulled by ID from the store and from
    bytes already present in <dir> (moves are detected).

    Without --force, nothing is written. stdout is the plan in c4m
    patch format: the C4 ID of <dir>'s current state, the entries that
    differ, and the target's ID. The two boundary IDs always appear;
    when <dir> already matches, they are equal and no entries appear.

    With --force:
      1. Every ID the target names must be resolvable; otherwise the
         missing IDs are listed on stderr and restore exits 1 without
         touching <dir>.
      2. If <dir> contains anything a snapshot cannot fully record
         (unreadable files, sockets, fifos, devices), restore refuses,
         lists the offenders on stderr, and exits 1 without touching
         <dir>.
      3. <dir>'s current state is snapshotted into the store — content,
         listings, and journal entry, durable — and that pre-image
         snapshot ID is printed as stdout line 1, always before the
         first modification.
      4. <dir> is reconciled, then verified (see VERIFICATION). Only
         then is the target ID printed as line 2.

VERIFICATION
    Verification is recomputation at the target's knowledge level.
    Snapshot-ID target: recorded modes and mtimes are applied
    explicitly (your umask is irrelevant), then the full-form listing
    is recomputed from the resulting tree and must reproduce the
    snapshot ID. Content-ID target: the content-form listing is
    recomputed and must reproduce the content ID — names, sizes,
    symlink targets, and bytes are verified; modes and times are
    platform-default metadata, meaning whatever file creation under
    your umask and clock produced — not recorded by the target, not
    claimed, and not verified. Line 2 prints only if recomputation
    reproduces the target ID exactly.

UNDO
    Line 1 reverses the operation:
        c4 restore --force <line-1> <dir>
    restores <dir> byte-exact, including recorded modes and times. The
    undo prints its own line 1, so it is itself undoable. There is no
    ref namespace to update or lose: the undo handle is the ID itself —
    printed on stdout, echoed in the stderr undo hint as a complete
    command, and recorded permanently in the store journal. `c4 log` is
    the reflog: a lost terminal does not lose the undo handle.

OUTPUT
    Dry run: the plan (c4m patch format) on stdout.
    --force: exactly two lines on stdout —
      line 1: pre-image snapshot ID of <dir> as it was
      line 2: the target's ID, verified from the resulting tree
    If <dir> already matches the target exactly, both lines are the
    same ID. If <dir> was absent or empty, line 1 is the empty
    description
    c459dsjfscH38cYeXXYogktxf4Cd9ibshE3BHUo6a58hBXmRQdZrAkZzsWcbWtDg5oQstpDuni4Hirj75GEmTc1sFT
    Restoring that ID empties the directory. Counts, warnings, and the
    undo command go to stderr.

DURABILITY
    Line 1 prints only after the pre-image is on stable media and
    always before the first modification. Line 2 prints only after the
    restored tree is verified and synced. If power fails between the
    lines, <dir> holds a mix of old and new whole files (no torn
    files); both end states are safe in the store — re-run the same
    command to finish, or restore line 1 to go back.

NOTES
    A description records names, sizes, modes, mtimes, symlink targets,
    hard links, sequences, and content IDs. It does not record
    ownership, extended attributes, ACLs, or special files; restore
    neither preserves nor restores those. Target entries with null IDs
    cannot be materialized: the rest is restored, the omissions are
    listed on stderr, and restore exits 2. restore never deletes <dir>
    itself: undoing a restore into a previously absent directory leaves
    an empty directory. Concurrent restores of the same directory are
    not coordinated: the store stays safe; the tree's final state is
    undefined.

EXIT STATUS
    0 plan emitted, or reconciled and verified
    1 refused: missing content, uncapturable entries, or unresolvable
      target — nothing modified
    2 reconciled with omissions (listed on stderr)

EXAMPLES
    c4 restore c461iQnu...igYz proj/          # preview
    c4 restore --force c461iQnu...igYz proj/  # apply, undoably
    c4 restore --force c461iQnu...igYz/src src/   # just one subtree
    c4 restore --force $(c4 id -s good/) bad/ # mirror good into bad
        # (mirroring requires id -s, so the content is in the store;
        #  piping `c4 id good/` alone fails the missing-content check)
    c4 restore --force c459dsjf...c1sFT tmp/  # empty tmp/, undoably

SEE ALSO
    c4 id -s (create snapshots), c4 log (find snapshot IDs),
    c4 diff (compare), c4 explain restore

C4-CAT(1)

NAME
    c4 cat - retrieve store objects by ID or ID/path; display c4m files

SYNOPSIS
    c4 cat [-e] [-r] <c4id[/path] | file.c4m>

DESCRIPTION
    With a C4 ID, fetches the object from the store and writes it to
    stdout. Every read is verified: the bytes must hash to the
    requested ID, or cat writes nothing and exits 1. A file ID yields
    the file's bytes. A listing ID (snapshot or content) yields the
    one-level child listing; with -r, directory entries are followed by
    their own listings, indented two spaces per level, fetched from the
    store.

    An ID may be followed by a slash-separated relative path:
        c4 cat <ID>/src/parser.go
    Each component descends one level by exact entry-name match in the
    stored listing, every level verified by rehash; the final component
    may name a file (its bytes) or a directory (its listing). This is
    sugar over the equivalent walk — cat the listing, read the entry's
    ID, cat that ID — and works at either knowledge level. An unknown
    name exits 1 with the missing component on stderr.

    A c4m file path displays the file; patch chains display resolved
    (use c4 log for history).

FLAGS
    -e, --ergonomic   Column-aligned c4m output
    -r, --recursive   Expand directory entries through the store

EXAMPLES
    c4 cat c461iQnu...igYz                 # one-level listing
    c4 cat c461iQnu...igYz/src/            # a subdirectory's listing
    c4 cat c461iQnu...igYz/src/parser.go > parser.go   # extract by name
    c4 cat -r c461iQnu...igYz              # whole tree, from the store
    c4 cat -r c461iQnu...igYz | c4 paths   # all paths
    c4 cat c45PDQdg...UNN > hello.txt      # extract by ID
    c4 cat -r ID | c4 id -q -              # recompute: verifies ID

C4-PATCH(1) / C4-DIFF(1)

SYNOPSIS

    c4 patch [-n N] [-e] <file.c4m>...

DESCRIPTION
    patch resolves patch chains: c4m text in, resolved c4m text out
    (stdout, or <dest.c4m>). patch reads and writes c4m text only; a
    directory argument exits 1 with:
        patch composes descriptions; to change a directory:
        c4 restore <target> <dir>
    -n N resolves to section N (1-based; 0 = final state).

    diff compares two states and emits a patch on stdout. Either side
    may be a directory, a c4m file, or a stored description ID
    (optionally ID/path). Directories are scanned at content level, or
    at the other side's level of detail when that side is a
    description.

C4-LOG(1)

NAME
    c4 log - list a patch chain's sections; default: the store journal

SYNOPSIS
    c4 log [<chain.c4m>...]

DESCRIPTION
    Lists one line per section: index, entry fields, section ID. With
    no arguments, reads the store journal <store>/log.c4m, in which the
    store records every ingest: snapshots from `c4 id -s`, stdin blobs
    from `| c4 -s`, and every pre-image taken by `c4 restore --force`.
    Each journal section is one entry:

        - <time> <listing-size> <name>.c4m <- <host:abs-path> <snapshot-id>

    followed by the chain boundary line. The journal is ordinary c4m
    text: any text tool can read it, and nothing in it is ever
    overwritten — history only.

    Appends are serialized with an advisory lock. Before appending, a
    writer truncates any trailing partial section; readers parse
    complete sections and warn once on stderr if a torn tail exists. A
    torn tail can only be the residue of an ingest that never printed
    its ID (the entry is appended before the ID prints), so nothing
    claimed is ever missing from the journal — and the converse holds
    after a crash: every complete journal line names a fully durable
    snapshot, even if its command never lived to print. If no append
    ever follows, a torn tail persists harmlessly; every complete
    section stays readable.

EXAMPLES
    c4 log                            # every snapshot this store holds
    c4 log /backup/store/log.c4m      # another store's journal

C4-GC(1)

NAME
    c4 gc - collect store objects unreachable from the roots

SYNOPSIS
    c4 gc [--force] [-v] [<roots.c4m>...]

DESCRIPTION
    Mark-and-sweep. Dry run unless --force. The roots are every ID
    recorded in any section of the store journal — full history, their
    listings at both levels of detail, and everything those name — plus
    any c4m files given as arguments. Arguments add roots; they never
    replace the journal roots, so nothing journaled is ever collected.
    Objects staged by an interrupted ingest that never printed are
    unrooted and appear in the dry-run report. To let old snapshots go,
    first truncate the journal explicitly:
        c4 split <store>/log.c4m <N> archive.c4m keep.c4m
    install keep.c4m as the journal (with snapshot activity stopped),
    then run c4 gc --force.

FLAGS
    --force     Delete unreferenced objects (default: report only)
    -v          List each unreferenced object

ledger.item: Two user-visible identity concepts: content ID and snapshot ID, one sentence each
ledger.reason: Unanimous across candidates and the provable minimum: T3 needs machine-independent sameness, T1/T2 need exact-record fidelity; no single ID answers both. Round-1 sims: all four personas used both correctly.

ledger.item: Content-form (stat-free) directory identity as the default for c4 id (-m c default)
ledger.reason: Fixes the standing determinism violation and is the only way T3 is answerable by string equality; frozen nulls, zero grammar change; observation stays one flag away (-m f).

ledger.item: Stat-bearing directory ID retained as any default identity
ledger.reason: Violates principle 10 and answers no question content ID + snapshot ID don't answer better; drift detection is diff's job.

ledger.item: Snapshot ID = ID of the full-observation root listing (flatten rule: description's canonical-text ID == root directory ID at the same knowledge level)
ledger.reason: A's found unification, verified against shipped WriteCanonical; makes self-ID, pipe law, and round-trip verification one rule and one object kind.

ledger.item: Separate whole-text description blob as the snapshot object (B/C mechanism)
ledger.reason: Mints a second object kind, invites the documented key-collision, loses per-directory Merkle dedup; the flatten unification makes it unnecessary.

ledger.item: Snapshot ingestion stores BOTH listing graphs (full-form and content-form) per directory
ledger.reason: cat/restore resolve either ID with no index or projection machinery; listings are tiny; closes A's content-ID-resolution gap.

ledger.item: Full-form listings carry child full-listing IDs; content-form carry child content IDs (line-local verification in both graphs)
ledger.reason: Every ID in any listing is the hash of the exact text it names; dissolves the 'invisible null-form transform' count against C.

ledger.item: Directory size field = total bytes of contained files, both forms
ledger.reason: st_size for directories is filesystem-dependent and would re-taint the content ID; sum is deterministic and informative.

ledger.item: Description-input dispatch pinned: .c4m argument and id's '-' parse as descriptions; unparseable .c4m errors; all other files are bytes; bare c4 stdin is raw bytes
ledger.reason: Kills content-sniffing nondeterminism (A blocking count 1); dispatch is a pure function of the argument name.

ledger.item: Files inside scanned trees are ALWAYS bytes — never parsed, canonicalized, or re-ID'd
ledger.reason: Shipped scan-time canonicalization (id.go:250-268) silently corrupts trees containing c4m-shaped files and falsifies T1 byte-exactness; hard-pinned on the surface.

ledger.item: id computes descriptions at their own knowledge level; -m projects downward only
ledger.reason: Restores snapshot-ID recomputability (B blocking count 2) while preserving the pipe law and cat -r round-trip verify (same rule via the flatten identity).

ledger.item: Patch chains resolve to final state before identification/display; -n reaches earlier states
ledger.reason: Pins the previously undefined chain-identity case deterministically using an existing flag.

ledger.item: -q requires an ID-bearing mode (c or f); errors under -m s/m
ledger.reason: An ID printed from bytes never hashed would be assertion, not verification (C prosecutor count 10).

ledger.item: id -s prints the snapshot ID alone on stdout; narration on stderr
ledger.reason: The ID is the machine datum (principle 9); the description text is exactly the losable artifact of complaint 1 and lives in the store instead.

ledger.item: id -s conflicts with -m (always full detail; content projection stored alongside)
ledger.reason: One canonical -s behavior; the content graph is always stored and the content ID always derivable.

ledger.item: Bare-invocation auto-ingest (bare 'c4 <path>' storing; stdin auto-store; -x escape)
ledger.reason: A cold user asking 'what is this?' must not silently write gigabytes (A count 6); uniform rule 'writes require -s or restore --force'. Breaking pre-freeze change, deliberate. Bare c4 <path> = read-only id.

ledger.item: Store journal <store>/log.c4m: ordinary c4m patch chain, one section per -s ingest (snapshots, stdin blobs, every restore pre-image, including empty ones)
ledger.reason: Store names its own roots; closes 'the ID itself is losable' and the lone-file-unrooted gc deletion; 'logged iff stored-at-your-request iff gc-protected' is one teachable sentence. Sims confirmed: journal rescued the lost-scrollback undo in T2.

ledger.item: Journal as basename-keyed catalog with current-state resolution
ledger.reason: Basename collision hands the user the WRONG pre-image (B blocking 3 / C blocking 1) — the safety feature becomes the destroyer; history listing evicts nothing and log is the verb named for it.

ledger.item: Bare 'c4 patch' as the catalog/recovery entry point
ledger.reason: Undiscoverable and mis-signaled: cold users will not run an apparently mutating verb with no arguments to read state (B count 12).

ledger.item: Journal torn-tail handling: writers repair under advisory lock before appending; readers warn on stderr (uniform c4m trailing-garbage behavior)
ledger.reason: At-rest file stays valid c4m with zero grammar change; no location-specific parse dialect. v2: repair algorithm and worst case pinned (see round-1 fold item).

ledger.item: Journal appends serialized by advisory lock; store puts concurrent-safe by construction (temp+fsync+rename, put-by-ID)
ledger.reason: Pins concurrency semantics at the exact file the durability contract rests on.

ledger.item: Durability protocol: temp+fsync(2)+rename per object; barrier; journal append+fsync; barrier; print. Printed => durable; unprinted => nothing claimed, tree untouched, store consistent, rerun idempotent
ledger.reason: Convergent and grounded in measured physics; per-file fsync keeps dedup's presence-implies-integrity valid after a crash. v2 adds the reader-side equivalence: complete journal line => durable snapshot.

ledger.item: Per-file F_FULLFSYNC durability
ledger.reason: Measured ~6.4ms/file (~3 minutes per 20k files) and buys nothing over the claim-point barrier; a promise nobody can act on.

ledger.item: Durability contract worded platform-neutrally; APFS/M-series numbers cited as measurements
ledger.reason: F_FULLFSYNC-specific semantics must not be the contract (B count 9); Linux supplies the equivalent. Round-1 sim re-flagged 'APFS-only numbers' — accepted tradeoff: unmeasured platforms get the ordering contract, never invented constants; surface now says so in one clause.

ledger.item: Restored trees get the strong promise: per-file fsync+rename, verify by recomputation at the target's knowledge level, barrier, then line 2 prints
ledger.reason: 'No tree durability promise' under-promises when the strong claim costs ~126us/file; between-lines state pinned as mix of whole files with both endpoints durable.

ledger.item: --no-fsync flag (anywhere)
ledger.reason: Safe was made fast (~126us/file); the mode would only multiply crash states.

ledger.item: restore is the ONLY tree-writing verb; patch returns to pure text algebra and errors on directories with a teaching message
ledger.reason: One implementation per idea; deletes the accident grammar of complaint 2. Sims: the teaching error was followed correctly.

ledger.item: restore is dry-run by default; --force applies (the single new flag)
ledger.reason: Principle 8's literal text, the gc --force precedent, and the founding wrong-usage user; always-apply rejected for pre-image completeness holes and suite inconsistency.

ledger.item: Dry-run plan output: boundary IDs always present, equal with no entries when already matching
ledger.reason: One parseable contract; the plan's first line is exactly what --force will print.

ledger.item: --force stdout = two lines: pre-image snapshot ID (durable, before first mutation) then verified target ID
ledger.reason: 'Backups durable before destruction begins' is the meaning of line 1, not a flag. Sims: all personas executed undo from line 1 without error.

ledger.item: Opt-out of the pre-image (--no-store broadening)
ledger.reason: Inheriting destructiveness into a benign shipped flag is the opposite of long-form-explicit (B count 5); the expensive case is the case the pre-image exists for; rm -rf remains the honest capture-free spelling.

ledger.item: --force refuses (exit 1, offenders listed, nothing touched) when <dir> contains entries a snapshot cannot fully capture
ledger.reason: Destruction demands complete capture (A blocking count 2); description alone stays partial-friendly (id warns, nulls, exit 2).

ledger.item: Fidelity boundary stated on the surface: records names/sizes/modes/mtimes/symlinks/hardlinks/sequences/content; NOT ownership/xattrs/ACLs/special files
ledger.reason: 'Byte-exact including recorded metadata' must not overpromise (C count 2); sidecar can extend later.

ledger.item: gc default roots = every ID in ANY journal section (full history, both graphs, closures); explicit args ADD roots; forgetting = explicit split then gc --force
ledger.reason: Closes gc-eats-undo and the history-vs-current ambiguity in favor of history; retention stays explicit composition, never policy.

ledger.item: restore targets are descriptions only (ID[/path], .c4m, or -); never a directory; mirroring = restore --force $(c4 id -s A) B with the missing-content trap named
ledger.reason: Direction confusion becomes unconstructible; the -s requirement and its reason stated where a cold user hits it. v2 extends the ID form with /path descent.

ledger.item: --source flag on restore (content from arbitrary directories, store-bypass mirroring)
ledger.reason: No success task needs it; store-mediated transfer is the architecture; same-volume clonefile ingest ~free (0.26s/14k); preserves the last flag of budget headroom. Revisit only on measured pain.

ledger.item: Empty description constant as pre-image of absent/empty dirs; undo of restore-into-absent-dir leaves an empty directory; no-op forced restore prints the same ID twice
ledger.reason: One always-resolvable fixed point replaces three special cases; the one-inode boundary stated honestly.

ledger.item: Concurrent restores of one directory: uncoordinated, stated on the surface (store safe, tree outcome undefined)
ledger.reason: ACCEPTED TRADEOFF, re-flagged by round-1 HN sim ('no file locking, just vibes') and standing: destination locking is coordination machinery a snapshot tool should not grow; the store is never at risk; the sentence is on the surface. Repeat friction on this point does not count.

ledger.item: Journal entry format: '- <UTC time> <listing size> <name>.c4m <- <host:abs-path> <snapshot ID>' + chain boundary per section
ledger.reason: Provenance flow link (frozen grammar) makes entries self-explanatory; same-basename trees disambiguated by origin path; collisions harmless under history-only semantics.

ledger.item: Legacy stat-bearing listings/IDs read as ordinary full-form listings; content IDs re-derived by c4 id -q; no permanent dual-rule verifier
ledger.reason: Under the merged model legacy IDs ARE full-form IDs; migration is one recompute; mixed-fleet T3 governed by the coordinated suite release.

ledger.item: Multi-store config: first store is the write store and holds the journal
ledger.reason: Pins the 'store line(s) plural' ambiguity in one sentence.

ledger.item: id/id -s exit 2 on partial scans; restore exits 2 when target null-ID entries were skipped
ledger.reason: Partial knowledge stays a valid, LOUD state: degraded output plus a distinct exit code.

ledger.item: id -s side effects enumerated on the surface: writes only inside the store (objects + journal); no .c4m file, nothing in the scanned tree or working directory, ever
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 1, personas 1+4 worst confusion): both doubted whether -s leaves artifacts outside the store; one surface sentence makes T1's 'delete artifacts outside the store' the empty set by construction.

ledger.item: Named references / ref namespace for snapshots and undo handles
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 2, git persona): ACCEPTED TRADEOFF. Refs are mutable state that can dangle, race, and lie; handles are IDs — stdout line 1, the stderr undo hint (a complete command), and a permanent journal entry. 'c4 log is the reflog' now stated in restore(1) UNDO. Repeat friction on wanting names does not count.

ledger.item: -q framed as output form only; identity level is chosen by -m (content default); stated in help and man
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 3, git persona worst confusion): user believed -q selects stability, inverting the git mental model; the stable ID is the default level, -q merely quiets. Wording fix, zero semantics change.

ledger.item: Progress narration on stderr: live file/byte count on a terminal, one summary line otherwise; stdout never carries narration
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 4, git persona T4): silent 6s runs read as hangs on bigger trees; stderr is the sanctioned narration channel (principle 9), non-contractual, zero flags.

ledger.item: ID/path store addressing: any store-resolved ID may be followed by /relative/path, descending listings by exact entry-name match, each level rehash-verified; on cat, restore targets, and diff sides
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 5, personas 2+4 T5): 'cat -r | grep' as the documented lookup is fragile (substring/metacharacter collisions) and forces manual ID extraction. Sugar over the documented walk; 0 new flags, 0 new verbs, not an identity concept; also yields subtree restore for free.

ledger.item: Restore verification pinned per knowledge level; 'platform-default metadata' defined (whatever creation under your umask/clock produced — not recorded, not claimed, not verified)
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 6, HN persona T1): 'verified against what — my umask?' was answerable but unstated; snapshot targets apply recorded modes/mtimes explicitly then recompute full-form; content targets recompute content-form only.

ledger.item: Journal repair algorithm and worst case pinned: writer truncates trailing partial section under the append lock; readers parse complete sections and warn once; torn tail <=> ingest that never printed; complete line after crash <=> fully durable snapshot; unclaimed objects unrooted (gc dry-run lists them)
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 7, HN persona T2): 'trust me it self-heals' needed the algorithm, the worst case, and the print-barrier tie-in; the equivalence also strengthens T4 (crash between journal barrier and print => c4 log shows a real, verifiable snapshot).

ledger.item: Hash-collision stance: ID equality is SHA-512 equality, stated once in IDENTITY; no per-line hedging; every store read rehash-verified
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 8, HN persona T3): ACCEPTED TRADEOFF. Collision resistance is the axiom of every content-addressed system; c4's claims are exactly as strong as SHA-512 and the surface now says so once, honestly, instead of dressing the assumption as an unconditional guarantee. Repeat friction does not count.

ledger.item: Timing model reconciled on the surface: ~130us/file + two ~5ms barriers is durability overhead BEYOND reading/hashing; worked example sums to the transcript's 6.1s (3.5s hash + 2.6s durability for 20,312 files / 4.8 GB)
ledger.reason: ROUND-1 FOLD (friction 9, HN persona T4): the constant and the transcript contradicted by 2x when 'overhead' was read as total; the man page now states what the constant excludes and shows the sum.

ledger.reason: New surface from the round-1 fold; the happy path is pinned, edges must be pinned in round 2 before freeze.

ledger.reason: Entry format assumes a scanned tree's basename and abs-path; stdin has neither. Cosmetic but must be deterministic. Round 2.

ledger.reason: Cosmetic; survived all four sims unchanged, so pressure is low; freeze in round 2.

ledger.reason: Networking/daemon is a declared non-goal; this surface claims local stores only. Non-blocking.

ledger.reason: GC policy is a declared non-goal; root rule is safe-by-default and the surgery recipe explicitly manual. Non-blocking implementation note.

result.summary_of_changes: Round-1 fold: 4 personas went 20/20 on the success tasks; 0 prosecutor blocking counts remain unresolved; 9 distinct novel friction events were folded. Two design changes: (1) ID/path store addressing (`c4 cat SNAP/src/parser.go`, restore targets, diff sides) — descends stored listings by exact entry name, each level rehash-verified; replaces the fragile `cat -r | grep` idiom flagged by two personas, at zero new flags/verbs/concepts. (2) Journal-line durability equivalence with the repair algorithm and worst case pinned: a complete journal line found after a crash names a fully durable snapshot (objects barriered before append); a torn tail belongs only to an ingest that never printed; repair = truncate the trailing partial section under the append lock; unclaimed objects are unrooted and shown by gc's dry run. Seven exactness fixes on the surface: id -s side effects enumerated (writes only inside the store — killing both cold-user worst confusions about phantom artifacts); -q reframed as output-form-only with content as the default identity level (git-user inversion); restore verification defined per knowledge level and 'platform-default metadata' given a definition; the timing model reconciled against its own transcript (durability overhead vs hash-bound total, with the worked 3.5s+2.6s≈6.1s sum shown); the SHA-512 axiom stated once in IDENTITY instead of implied as an unconditional guarantee; stderr progress narration added (TTY live count, pipe summary); and 'c4 log is the reflog / there is no ref namespace' stated in restore(1) UNDO. Ledger updated: 9 new decided items tagged ROUND-1 FOLD, named-refs rejected as an accepted tradeoff, hash-axiom and concurrent-restore items explicitly marked accepted tradeoffs so repeat friction stops counting, and 3 new open items (ID/path edges, stdin-blob journal naming, progress format). Budget unchanged: 2 identity concepts, 1 new verb (restore), 1 new flag (--force), 0 grammar changes, 0 deps.
open_items: Pin ID/path edge semantics before freeze: component naming a symlink or file mid-path (error vs follow-never), trailing-slash form (require for directory listings?), and whether .c4m-file targets may also take /path descent.
Define the journal entry's <name>.c4m and origin fields for stdin blob ingests (| c4 -s), which have no basename or abs-path; must be deterministic.
Pin the stderr progress format and TTY-detection rule once (non-contractual narration, but agents benefit from a stable shape).
Freeze the exact c4 log column layout (survived all four sims unchanged; low pressure).

Carried non-goals: journal semantics for non-local (s3/remote) stores; retention recipe concurrency (stop writers during split, gc holds append lock); fidelity sidecar for xattrs/ownership/ACLs as an external structure.

Round-2 sim note: keep T1's wording ('delete every file the snapshot produced outside the store') — the surface now answers it explicitly ('-s writes only inside the store'), so it becomes a test that the sentence lands rather than a trap.
